A left-opening horizontal parabola has the form

\[
(y-k)^2=-4p(x-h)
\]

where \((h,k)\) is the vertex and \(p>0\).

If you mean the vertex is **two units to the right of the origin**, i.e. \((2,0)\), and you choose the standard width \(p=1\), then the equation is

\[
\boxed{y^2=-4(x-2)}
\]

If instead the vertex is two units to the left of the origin, \((-2,0)\), then it would be

\[
\boxed{y^2=-4(x+2)}
\]

Without more information, there are infinitely many left-opening parabolas whose vertices are two units from the origin.<|im_end|>
